knowledge.progressSummary: PROGRESS: verified structural core of the r-product framework (primes valid all r, F_r>=pi lower bound, descending chain, r=1/r=2 endpoints, C_r>=0); open asymptotic constant isolated as unproven prop. 0 sorry 0 axiom. PR #34939.
insights: Any finset of primes satisfies the r-product condition for EVERY r (a prime dividing a product of distinct primes must equal one of them) — no size threshold needed, generalizing the parent's r=2-only large-primes lemma
F_r(n) >= pi(n) is now a VERIFIED theorem (primePi_le_F_r) via le_csSup with explicit BddAbove witness n=|[1,n]|; the parent Erdos793Problem only asserted this axiomatically

The r-product conditions form a DESCENDING CHAIN in r: satisfiesConditionR A r implies it for all r'<=r, provided r < |A| (a short divisible product pads up to length r inside A minus {a}); the size bound is necessary since the condition is vacuous when |A|<=r
r=1 recovers the classical primitive-set condition; r=2 recovers the parent noDividesProduct — so F_r faithfully interpolates between primitive-set counting and Erdos #793
nextSteps: Upgrade primePi_le_F_r to a verified SECOND-ORDER lower bound F_r(n) >= pi(n) + c*n^{2/(r+1)} via an explicit smooth-number / composite construction
Investigate monotonicity or structure of the open constant C_r in r, and its degeneration as r->infinity (exponent 2/(r+1)->0)
